unit.name: Prompt chaining, prompt tests, and LLM judges
unit.description: Explains how to decompose complex prompts into chains, why intermediate outputs aid debugging, and how prompt tests and LLM-as-judge rubrics scale evaluation.
unit.summary: Chaining is separated from chain-of-thought: instead of only asking for step-by-step reasoning, it splits a complex workflow into multiple prompts whose outputs feed later prompts [ts=1933s]. The instructor uses a customer-review response example to show that a single prompt can work but hides failure modes across extraction, outline creation, and final response writing [ts=1957s]. Chaining improves control because intermediate outputs reveal which prompt should be optimized, though longer chains add latency [ts=2007s]. Prompt testing starts with human review of generated outputs across test cases, then can be scaled using tools or LLM judges [ts=2286s]. LLM judges can perform pairwise comparison, single-answer grading, reference-guided comparison, or rubric-based scoring, and rubrics themselves can be few-shot calibrated [ts=2386s].

key_points.text: Prompt chaining means splitting a workflow into multiple prompt calls whose outputs become inputs for later calls.
Separating prompts allows each intermediate step to be debugged and optimized independently.
A chain can be evaluated both end-to-end and at intermediate outputs such as an outline or extraction result.
Long chains can be undesirable in latency-sensitive applications.
Prompt testing can compare a baseline prompt, a refined prompt, and their generated outputs on representative test cases.
LLM judges can compare two candidate outputs, grade a single answer, or apply a rubric to assess quality.

kp_catalog.name: Prompt chaining
kp_catalog.description: A workflow pattern where a complex task is decomposed into multiple prompt calls and intermediate outputs are inspected, reused, and optimized.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Prompt chaining supports reliable LLM workflows after prompt design is understood.

kp_catalog.name: Prompt testing and LLM-as-judge
kp_catalog.description: Methods for evaluating prompt outputs with test cases, human review, automated platforms, pairwise comparison, single-answer grading, references, and rubrics.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The lecture connects prompt improvement to systematic evals and later reuses LLM judges in agentic workflow assessment [ts=2386s].
